Q1: Bio-Perge shows internationally recognized, significant hazards (Tier 1) for environmental impact, inhalation, oral exposure, and dermal/eye contact. Potential hazards related to carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive toxicity (CMR) are indicated by more current data (Tier 2). However, there is insufficient data (Tier 4) to confidently assess its endocrine disruption and organ/systemic hazards.
Q2: Bio-Perge is not listed on any official Lists of Concern or Lists of Low Hazard. This, combined with several data deficient hazard categories, suggests it may not have been extensively evaluated or is not in sufficiently common use to be included on such lists.
Q3: Bio-Perge is relatively well-characterized, boasting 7073 scientific references, considerably above the median for petrochemicals, and has a defined molecular formula. While its 'Mixture' classification doesn't imply an undefined substance, the presence of two data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard categories for endocrine disruption and organ/systemic effects indicates some incompleteness in its hazard profile.
